episode.title: Plan the Dive, Manage the Risk
episode.description: Rina talks with Marco Silva: Plan the Dive, Manage the Risk.

feed.description: Scuba diving stories and skills: safety, marine life, travel, and calm thinking underwater.
feed.title: Below the Surface

bullets: Dive planning is fundamentally risk management, not paperwork, because it addresses the gas not used and the ascent not rushed.
The most harmful incidents are those not anticipated or named on the boat, so all potential failures must be named and planned for in advance.
A dive is a system of interacting elements—depth, gas, team, current—where accidents arise from their interactions, not isolated numbers.
Reviewing a decade of incident reports confirms that planning for system-level interactions prevents failures.
Dive planning and portfolio management share the same discipline: systems of correlated risk that can be controlled only when described in advance.
The one risk you can describe in advance is the one you can actually control, because description enables anticipation and mitigation.
Accidents live in the space between elements, not in any single variable, so planning must consider the whole system.
Underwater stress stems from surprise and lack of rehearsal, not inherent difficulty, so practice transforms alarming situations into manageable ones.
